policy.copyright_rule: Do not reproduce full copyrighted standards, books or papers. Store metadata, official links, concise engineering summaries, page/section references when available, and only short permitted excerpts.
policy.release_rule: External evidence may close a technical requirement only when model/application compatibility is demonstrated; otherwise keep HOLD.

sources.title: IEC 60909-0 - Short-circuit currents in three-phase a.c. systems - Part 0: Calculation of currents
sources.edition_note: current project basis; verify licensed edition before issue
sources.application: Method for Ik/Icc, initial symmetrical current, peak current and equipment duty.
facts: Fault level is a property of the upstream network and impedances, not a default supplied by a breaker manufacturer.
Final Icu/Icw/Ipk verification requires calculated or declared prospective fault current at the installation point.

sources.title: Electrical Installation Guide
sources.application: Short-circuit impedance method, conductor sizing workflow, voltage drop, protective-device coordination.
facts: Conductor selection requires load current, installation method, ambient correction, voltage drop and short-circuit withstand.
Short-circuit current downstream can be derived from upstream fault level plus intervening impedance.

sources.title: IEC 61439-1:2020 - Low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies - General rules
sources.application: Assembly ratings, verification, temperature-rise, declared characteristics including short-circuit withstand as applicable.
facts: Temperature-rise verification is part of assembly verification.
Power supplies and UPS incorporated into an assembly remain subject to their product standards plus the assembly integration requirements.

sources.title: IEC 60529 - Degrees of protection provided by enclosures (IP Code)
sources.application: IP66 requirement and verification of enclosure after modifications.
facts: IP rating is verified by standardized tests.
After installing cooling equipment/cut-outs, the final assembled enclosure must still have evidence for the claimed IP degree.

sources.title: Harmony ST6 - Electrical Specifications
sources.application: 24 Vdc UPS load and thermal model.
facts: Rated input 24 Vdc.
Input range 19.2 to 28.8 Vdc.
Maximum power 12.6 W.
Inrush current up to 30 A.

sources.title: Phaseo regulated power supply
sources.application: 24 Vdc supply sizing and heat dissipation.
facts: 24 Vdc, 10 A, 240 W class.
Previously verified engineering data includes approximately 31 W full-load loss; reverify against current official datasheet at release.

sources.title: CBI2420A Data Sheet
sources.application: DC UPS/charger candidate for all 24 Vdc loads and 30 min autonomy.
facts: 24 Vdc system; high-current DC UPS/charger.
Final battery sizing depends on measured/calculated total protected load, temperature, ageing and allowed depth of discharge.

sources.title: SIMATIC ET 200SP AI 4xI 2-wire 4-20 mA HART High Feature
sources.application: 67 installed AI channels.
facts: 4 HART-capable current input channels per module.
17 modules provide 68 channels, covering 67 installed channels with one spare channel.
Exact BaseUnits and power-segment architecture still require final configuration.

sources.title: SCALANCE XC208G
sources.application: Managed Layer 2 eight-port Gigabit switch matching FD requirement.
facts: Eight RJ45 Gigabit ports and redundant DC supply are consistent with project requirement; exact datasheet must be archived at release.

sources.title: TEMP-WM Wall Mount Temperature Transmitter
sources.application: User reference only.
facts: Wall mount, loop-powered 4-20 mA class, compatible with 24 Vdc supply range.
Official material located does not establish HART; therefore it cannot satisfy the frozen HART requirement by itself.

sources.title: HART Temperature Transmitters
sources.application: Possible HART transmitter paired with room sensor/RTD assembly.
facts: Two-wire 4-20 mA with HART is available in NOVUS HRT transmitter families.
These are head/DIN-rail transmitters, so an ambient wall sensing assembly must be engineered separately.

sources.title: SITRANS TF320 Field Temperature Transmitter
sources.application: Industrial HART temperature transmitter alternative.
facts: 4-20 mA and HART 7 family.
Field/wall/pipe-mounted enclosure concept, but not a compact room sensor; requires a suitable ambient sensing element and mounting arrangement.

sources.title: TVR Smart Controls - Gateway literature
sources.application: Research path for user requirement: only official Trane 24 Vdc gateway.
facts: Trane officially lists TCONTSMCB24V under Gateways for TVR Smart.
Model name alone is not proof of supply voltage/protocol; PDF technical content must be extracted and validated before freezing.

sources.title: TVR Smart gateway family
sources.application: Alternative official Trane gateways if TCONTSMCB24V does not meet requirements.
facts: Official Trane page lists multiple gateway models and direct product literature links.

sources.title: ClimaSys Cooling Unit Guide
sources.application: Closed-loop cooling at 40 C while preserving enclosure sealing.
facts: Closed-loop cooling is conceptually compatible with maintaining a sealed cabinet.
Manufacturer installation requirements found previously reference minimum enclosure sealing levels, but do not by themselves prove the final modified assembly remains IP66.
Final selection requires thermal-load calculation and explicit IP66 assembly/interface evidence.

sources.title: Infrared Gas Transmitter
sources.application: Industrial candidate for CO2 0-5000 ppm + 4-20 mA + HART.
facts: Research located a low-range CO2 configuration up to 5000 ppm with analog output and HART option.
It is an industrial gas detector rather than a conventional HVAC wall IAQ sensor; project suitability must be approved.

sources.title: Omniguard Gas Detector Model 3100
sources.application: Alternative CO2 transmitter with HART.
facts: Published options include CO2 0-5000 ppm and 4-20 mA/HART configuration.
HVAC-room suitability, availability and acceptance still need manufacturer/submittal verification.

sources.author: Phase to Phase
sources.title: Networks for Electricity Distribution - Chapter 8: Short-circuit calculations
sources.application: Independent explanation of IEC 60909 impedance method and voltage factor c.
facts: The method requires source/network impedance or short-circuit power/current and impedances of transformers/cables.
Supports the conclusion that 220 V alone is insufficient to derive the prospective fault current.

sources.title: Short-Circuit Calculation and Overcurrent Relay Protection in AC Microgrids: A Review
sources.application: Background on IEC 60909 and limitations where converter-interfaced sources dominate.
facts: IEC 60909 remains a core standardized method; model limitations matter in converter-dominated systems.
For this small automation panel, the main practical need remains accurate upstream source and cable data.

sources.title: IEC-oriented cable sizing workflow
sources.application: Cross-check workflow only; not primary design authority.
facts: Final cable section must satisfy ampacity, derating, voltage drop, short-circuit withstand and protective-device coordination.
Use IEC 60364-5-52/IEC 60287 as primary normative basis.

open_research_tasks: Extract technical content from official Trane TCONTSMCB24V PDF and confirm actual supply voltage, protocol and compatible TVR families.
Find a true room/wall temperature transmitter assembly with 4-20 mA + HART suitable for HVAC occupied spaces, or define wall sensor + remote HART transmitter architecture.
Validate an industrial CO2 0-5000 ppm + 4-20 mA + HART product for occupied-room HVAC application, including supply, accuracy, calibration and lifecycle.
Close exact CPU, BaseUnits and ET 200SP power-segment architecture.
Calculate full 24 Vdc load and battery capacity for 30 min autonomy.
Perform enclosure thermal calculation and select ClimaSys/equivalent with final IP66 evidence.
Obtain upstream fault-level data for IEC 60909 calculation; manufacturer breaker ratings cannot replace site Ik/Icc.
